message.content:
**Hydrogen (H)** – the simplest and most abundant element in the universe – has a rich set of physical, chemical, and nuclear properties. Below is a concise overview grouped by category.

| Category | Property | Value / Description |
|----------|----------|---------------------|
| **Basic Atomic Data** | Atomic number | 1 |
| | Atomic mass (average) | 1.008 u |
| | Electron configuration | 1s¹ |
| | Isotopes | H‑1 (protium), H‑2 (deuterium), H‑3 (tritium) |
| | Ionization energy | 13.598 eV (first ionization) |
| | Electron affinity | –0.754 eV (negative, meaning it does not readily accept an electron) |
| | Electronegativity (Pauling) | 2.20 |
| | Atomic radius | ~31 pm (covalent) |
| | Van der Waals radius | ~120 pm |
| **Physical Properties (at 25 °C, 1 atm)** | State | Gas |
| | Density | 0.08988 g L⁻¹ |
| | Boiling point | –252.87 °C (−423.17 °F) |
| | Melting point | –259.16 °C (−434.69 °F) |
| | Specific heat capacity (gas) | 14.304 J mol⁻¹ K⁻¹ |
| | Molar volume | 22.414 L mol⁻¹ |
| | Refractive index | 1.000132 (at 589 nm) |
| | Speed of sound | ~1270 m s⁻¹ (in H₂ gas) |
| | Solubility in water | ~1.6 g L⁻¹ (at 25 °C) |
| **Chemical Properties** | Bond type | Diatomic (H₂) with a single covalent bond |
| | Bond dissociation energy | 436 kJ mol⁻¹ (≈4.48 eV per bond) |
| | Oxidation states | +1 (most common), –1 (hydride), 0 (molecular) |
| | Reactivity | Highly flammable; reacts with oxygen to form water (combustion). Forms hydrides with many metals. |
| | Acid–base behavior | Acts as a weak acid (H⁺ donor) in aqueous solution; forms hydronium (H₃O⁺). |
| | Redox behavior | Can be oxidized to H⁺ or reduced to H₂ gas. |
| | Spectral lines | Lyman series (UV), Balmer series (visible), Paschen series (IR). |
| **Nuclear Properties** | Nuclear spin | ½ (protium), 0 (deuterium), ½ (tritium) |
| | Magnetic moment | 2.792847 µ_N (protium), 0 (deuterium), 5.585694 µ_N (tritium) |
| | Half‑life (tritium) | 12.32 years |
| | Nuclear reactions | Fusion (p + p → d + e⁺ + ν_e), (p + d → He‑3 + γ), (p + t → He‑4 + n). |
| **Applications & Uses** | Energy | Fuel cell hydrogen, rocket propellant, fusion research. |
| | Industrial | Production of ammonia (Haber process), methanol, hydrogenation reactions. |
| | Analytical | Used as a tracer in isotope‑ratio mass spectrometry. |
| | Medical | MRI contrast agents (tritium labeling). |
| | Environmental | Hydrogen fuel cells produce only water as exhaust. |

---

### Quick Takeaways

- **Lightest element**: Hydrogen is the lightest and most abundant element in the cosmos.
- **Diatomic gas**: Exists as H₂ under normal conditions; highly flammable.
- **Isotopic diversity**: Protium (stable), deuterium (stable, heavier), tritium (radioactive, used in fusion).
- **Key role in chemistry**: Forms hydrides with metals, acts as a proton donor in acids, and participates in redox reactions.
- **Energy frontier**: Central to hydrogen fuel cells and nuclear fusion research.

Feel free to ask if you’d like deeper details on any specific property or application!
